about: How long pairtime keeps each kind of data, from DESIGN 4.4. This file is the one copy the code reads. The privacy notice at /privacy renders its retention table from it, and pairtimed's retention jobs take their periods, tables and columns from it. In kept, {days} stands for the entry's days and {window} for the spot-check window, so a number is never written twice. Every table pairtimed's migrations create belongs to an entry, as its job's table or in its tables, or is listed in no_personal_data. A job or hold with awaits set is off until the work package named there creates its table, and that package removes awaits.

spot_check_window.provisional: DESIGN 4.4 and 13.2 item 4: 12 months after the decision until Hack Club HQ sets the spot-check window

entries.data: The text of your prompts, and the agent's final reply to each one
entries.kept: {days}, or until a submission that covers them is decided, whichever is later. You can shorten this, or turn off "keep prompt text"

entries.data: Your AI tool's transcripts and output
entries.kept: Not copied. pairtime reads them where your AI tool keeps them, so the tool's own setting applies (Claude Code keeps them for 30 days unless you change it)

entries.data: File paths kept for your recaps, and the commands your agent ran
entries.kept: {days}

entries.data: Presence and focus samples, typing counts if you turned on the typing module, and prompt similarity sketches (MinHash)
entries.kept: {days}

entries.data: Ledger records and batch roots: the sealed log of what pairtime recorded
entries.kept: {days}, or longer while a submission that uses them is inside its spot-check window ({window})

entries.data: Minute buckets
entries.kept: {days}. Daily totals and coach records stay until you delete them

entries.data: Your device key
entries.kept: Until you uninstall pairtime or the key is replaced

entries.data: Your account: your Hack Club Auth ID, Slack ID and handle, your email address (stored encrypted), and your GitHub user ID if you link GitHub
entries.kept: While your account exists

entries.data: Your devices: a random device ID, the OS family, the pairtime build, and the names and versions of your AI tools
entries.kept: Until you remove the device, then {days} more

entries.data: The IP address each upload comes from, and its TLS fingerprint (JA4)
entries.kept: {days}, then deleted outright, not shortened

entries.data: Minute buckets: the credited and uncredited seconds of each minute, by project key
entries.kept: Per-minute detail for {days}, the furthest back a submission can reach. After that only daily totals per project stay, for as long as your account exists

entries.data: Witness rows and batch roots: the hash of each upload batch, and when the server received it
entries.kept: {days}. Rows that a submission uses stay until its spot-check window closes ({window})

entries.data: Commit records (commit IDs, times and line counts, with file paths only as keyed hashes) and project fingerprints
entries.kept: While your account exists

entries.data: Keyed hashes of the Hackatime project names you link to a program
entries.kept: Until you unlink the program

entries.data: Backups, only if you turn them on: your device key, locked with your recovery code, and encrypted copies of your ledger and vault
entries.kept: Until you turn backups off or delete your account. Backup segments older than {days} are deleted

entries.data: What you reveal when you submit hours: the records behind them, the prompts drawn for review, and any risk flags
entries.kept: Until the spot-check window closes ({window}). You can delete any revealed item yourself, at once

entries.data: Reviewer decisions and the reasons for cuts, written without personal data
entries.kept: As long as the program's record of the submission exists in Hack Club's Unified DB

entries.data: The evidence access log: who opened your submitted evidence, and when. You can see it
entries.kept: 2 years

entries.data: Notes from an audit call. Calls are never recorded
entries.kept: As long as the decision they belong to

entries.data: After you delete your account: a minimal fraud record (your Hack Club Auth ID, the verdict, its date and a reason category)
entries.kept: For a period Hack Club sets, which isn't decided yet. The deletion report lists it as kept

entries.data: Day roots: one hash a day over every batch the server received, with a count, published in the public pairtime-witness repository
entries.kept: Permanently. They hold only hashes and a daily count
